avalancheActivity.comment:
Fresh snow will fall on the existing snowpack in the high mountains. Small drifts of wind-blown snow will form, particularly near ridges, where even a small additional load could trigger a small slab avalanche. Terrain features will not yet be completely buried, so even a small avalanche may be more dangerous than it would be under a thicker snowpack.
On the steepest slopes, some small to medium-sized avalanches of dry, unconsolidated snow are expected whilst it is snowing.
avalancheActivity.highlights: Mainly above 1,600 metres, some fresh snow with moderate winds

snowpackStructure.comment: Up to 30 cm of snow fell in the high mountains a week ago. Isolated avalanches of loose snow were triggered on steep slopes. Today, Wednesday, it is snowing again. Overnight, there was light snowfall down to the lowlands; during the day, the snow line rose above 1,600 m. The thin, old snowpack below this altitude has become saturated. Higher up, with a moderate south-westerly wind, up to 10 cm of fresh snow has fallen.

tendency.highlights: It will remain cold and mostly cloudy. Light precipitation will ease off by Friday morning. The snow cover will melt only slowly.

weatherForecast.comment:
On Wednesday afternoon and overnight into Thursday, precipitation will intensify, and the snow line will drop to the lowlands in the second half of the night. Where warmer air lingers for a few hours in the low mountain ranges, a layer of ice, known as ‘žled’, may form on the ground.
Above 1,600 metres, 30 cm of fresh snow will fall by morning; less at lower altitudes.
On Thursday morning, a strong south-easterly wind will blow for a few hours, before easing off by midday, except in the Primorska region, where the bora will continue to blow for at least a few more days. Elsewhere, it will remain cloudy and cold, with the zero isotherm near the lowlands and temperatures around -2 °C between 1,500 m and 2,000 m. Precipitation will ease off during the day, with a further 10 cm of snow expected to fall everywhere by the evening.
